clue.text: 9 that was, according to 5 — a musical sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the stage show's title is only heard, so its spoken form gives the letters entered

parts.note: Grease is the 1970s rock-and-roll stage musical, later a film

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle about a poet's line, tagged with a passing note about music.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is GLORY and 5 is EDGAR ALLAN POE, whose poem To Helen has 'the glory that was Greece'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's line pairs glory with the ancient Hellenic nation, so the cross-reference leads to that country.

clue.text: Good one for oratory, yet maybe takes up a lot of space

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the gift of the gab is a talent for oratory

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word might be in another order, so it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A good speaker may still ramble on and take up room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes up' links wordplay to definition; 'yet' is rearranged to YTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigabyte is about a billion bytes of computer storage, a large amount of memory space.

clue.text: Point for joker holding on to what will pay

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: holding means the comedian's name contains the short word

parts.note: a comic is a joker
on taken as written

explanation.surface: A joker holds on to a scheme that will pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic proposition is one that is profitable, that will pay its way.

clue.text: Outlaw celebrated by Georgie Fame with carthorses around?

definitions.meaning: Georgie Fame's 1967 hit was The Ballad of Bonnie and ..., the American outlaws
Clydesdales, the heavy Scottish carthorses, come from the valley of this river

explanation.surface: A gangster song with farm horses in the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Clyde Barrow was Bonnie Parker's partner in crime, and the Scottish river gave the Clydesdale horse its name.

clue.text: Game heard to be in prospect, according to poet

indicators.note: heard means the name of the racket game is only spoken, giving the first part of the poet's surname

parts.note: tennis is a racket game
a fixture that is on is going ahead, expected to happen

explanation.surface: A poet seems to be forecasting a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The game's name is heard, not spelt, then ON follows; 'according to' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote In Memoriam.

clue.text: Poet on parade with legal characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the preceding words, freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet marches past alongside lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters, so the letters of ON PARADE and LEGAL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer of The Raven and Tales of Mystery was a celebrated poet.

clue.text: No painter of Delft could tell what 5's 12 said

parts.note: Vermeer was the painter of Delft, so 'no Vermeer' is a rough spoken match

explanation.surface: A Dutch master who refuses to paint, quoting a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is Poe and 12 is his RAVEN, whose only word is the repeated refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poe's poem the bird answers every question with the same single-word refrain meaning not ever again.

clue.text: Girl and boy not finally down in the mouth

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name

indicators.note: not finally means dropping the final letter

parts.note: Ivan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Two young people feeling glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down in the mouth' means depressed, but here it is literal: what flows down inside the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Saliva is the spit that flows down within the mouth.

clue.text: Being a detective suggests silence with entry of 20 from Keats

parts.note: Keats's La Belle Dame sans Merci gives silence as 'And no birds sing'
20 across is BIRDS

explanation.surface: A sleuth hinting at quiet by quoting a Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as NO SING, with BIRDS put in, gives Keats's line for silence; 'from Keats' names the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing around means snooping or investigating, as a detective does.

clue.text: Singular 20 on beginning of Georgie Fame

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of the singer's first name

parts.note: 20 is BIRDS; one bird of that kind is a lory, a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A note about the jazz singer Georgie Fame's early career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fame' looks like part of the singer's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory and fame are synonyms for renown and public honour.

clue.text: Without much of a dance, breaks the ice perhaps with lots and lots of potential

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a thaw melts ice, one way of breaking it up

indicators.note: much of a word is most of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the gavot is an old spelling of the gavotte, a French court dance

explanation.surface: Someone wins a crowd over without dancing, showing huge promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Breaks the ice' wants to mean easing social tension, but it is the melting of a thaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A megavolt is a million volts, so megavolts are huge amounts of electrical potential difference.

clue.text: Does "Deceived by magnetism" mean a mess is being made of it?

definitions.text: a mess is being made of it

indicators.note: deceived suggests the letters are tricked into another order

explanation.surface: A question whether falling for a magnetic personality means things are going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'Does' are linking words; the anagram uses MAGNETISM plus MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismanagement is poor handling of affairs, the making of a mess of something.

clue.text: I'll see if there are chemicals in Boris — one's uncertain

definitions.text: I'll see if there are chemicals

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters are unsettled and so rearranged

parts.note: one's taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A politician named Boris is unsure whether chemicals are present.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written as the device speaking for itself: a sensor that detects chemical substances in a biological setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A biosensor is a detecting device combining a biological element with a sensor to register chemical substances.

clue.text: Bird used to be very hungry

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to be ravenous, to feed greedily; 'used to' marks the sense as archaic

explanation.surface: A bird that once had a large appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: This is also the bird of Poe's famous poem, which 6 refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the large black corvid; the archaic verb meant to have a voracious appetite.

clue.text: Kite flown in place of golf ball after I get a pound inside

indicators.note: inside says the run of pieces sits within the golf venue

parts.note: Troon is a Scottish seaside town with a championship golf links

indicators.note: ball after the other pieces means it comes last

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
ball taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer swaps a ball for a kite on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly a kite is to float an idea to test reaction, hence the definition. TROON is a golf town in Ayrshire, Scotland, that hosts the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial balloon is a tentative proposal put out to gauge opinion, just as flying a kite tests reaction.

clue.text: Pine for old golf club for use at diabolical table

parts.note: to pine for is to long for
a spoon was an old wooden golf club with a lofted face

explanation.surface: Missing an old golf club used at a devilish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says he who sups with the devil should have a long spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial utensil you need when dining with the devil, to keep him at arm's length.

clue.text: To remove wrong ideas of God is a bus exposé

indicators.note: of points to letters drawn from part of the following words

explanation.surface: An exposé of religion turns up on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'God' through 'is a bus' to the start of 'exposé', which itself hints at uncovering.
explanation.definitionFit: To disabuse someone is to free them from a false belief or mistaken idea.

clue.text: Spare the criminal with a record

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters have been wrongly treated, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to show mercy to a criminal who has form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links; 'criminal' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is an informal American term for a person's criminal record.

clue.text: Old coin, Indian and Burmese, in a novel

parts.note: the anna was a former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee
the Karen are a people of Burma (Myanmar)
in taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of exotic odds and ends found inside a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's long work about an adulterous aristocrat is one of the great Russian novels.

clue.text: Counter beginners' account at the Guardian

parts.note: AB, the opening letters of the alphabet, are what beginners learn
a newspaper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: Beginners' bookkeeping at the newspaper's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a verb or a shop fitting; it is the device for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used as a counting device.

clue.text: University kingdom?

definitions.meaning: ... University is in Uxbridge, west London
'kingdom' is his middle name, so the surname follows it

explanation.surface: A one-word question about a country with a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel University is named after the engineer Isambard Kingdom, whose surname follows that middle name.

clue.text: Prison's what rejects are for

definitions.meaning: bird is slang for a prison sentence (rhyming slang bird-lime, time); prison's read as prison is
worthless things are said to be 'for the' winged creatures of this name

explanation.surface: Prison is where rejects end up.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird means serving time, and the idiom 'for the birds' means worthless or fit to be thrown out.

clue.text: Second sight where French girl's wedding's in the past

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is second sight
ou is French for where
Sal is a girl's name; with the possessive it gives these letters

explanation.surface: A French girl had a premonition of her own wedding long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like S; the whole phrase 'Second sight' gives the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousals is an old-fashioned word for a marriage or betrothal ceremony.

clue.text: Personal pronouns of the old school

parts.note: us is a first-person plural pronoun
her is a third-person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A grammar point of an old-fashioned kind.
explanation.walkthrough: An usher was formerly an assistant schoolmaster, so the definition is a person of the old school, literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an under-master at a school was called by this title, now archaic.

clue.text: African gives Spanish shouts during French leave

indicators.note: during means the cheers come in the middle of the leave

ole is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: An African cheers in Spanish while taking a French holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French leave' usually means slipping away unannounced; here it is literally the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Congolese describes a person from the Congo in central Africa.

clue.text: 5's 22 fell — Bingo!

definitions.meaning: Poe's story is The Fall of the ... of Usher, 22 being USHER
the shout a bingo player makes on completing a card

clue.text: Some lines in mental health show the opposite of freshness

parts.note: sanity is soundness of mind

indicators.note: some of a word is a part of it, here its first two letters

explanation.definitionFit: Salinity means saltiness, and salt water is the opposite of fresh water.

clue.text: Enthusiastic model following Forest

indicators.note: following means the model comes after the woodland

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire and in As You Like It

explanation.surface: An eager model trails along behind a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager, a close synonym of keen.
